checks.a1_scope: The local A1 foundation specification in blueprint 4.0 governs. This is the first A1 writing batch. No official A1 task comparison, exam-format claim or equivalence verdict applies. There are no same-level writing exemplars in the current catalogue. A separate first-batch target check remains the coordinator’s next step.
checks.contract: Exactly nine original messages, two tiny content goals and one understandable-language criterion each, one drawing brief and Dutch alt each, correct A1/bericht/a1-schrijven/a1-practice metadata. Models contain 8-13 words and prompts 24-36, within the local 8-25 and <=55 limits. No retired type, generated media, revision, official score or KNM facts.
checks.language: Every final prompt, bilingual criterion, sample, quote, model, starter, brief and alt was read. Models have two short main-clause sentences of four to seven words. Familiar concrete nouns include ui, lepel, sokken and kom, all supported by a picture/alt. No required reason, advanced tense, subordinate response, greeting sequence or narrative.
checks.sample_quotes: Every sample has exactly one null in a content-goal position. Its two non-null quotes are exact substrings. Every sample is comprehensible despite its deliberate beginner verb-form error; grammar perfection is not the language gate. Each sample’s other wording was checked for accidental satisfaction of the null goal.
checks.criteria_and_models: For each item the two criteria trace to the prompt and visible detail. The model explicitly meets both. Alternative opinions, food choices, short phrasings and understandable learner variants remain acceptable. One sentence may meet two content goals where both intentions are clear.
checks.starters: All 27 fragments were read in criterion order, tested for natural completions and found incomplete. They leave the required facts to the learner. Criteria did not change, so the author starter file passes unchanged and no proposed-starters file is needed.
checks.diversity: All 66 current writing catalogue prompts and 16 nearby full records were compared. No matching complete premise or same-part slug collision. The first two messages share an object-identification/request shape but differ in workplace help versus correction of a shop purchase. Other acts include opinion, preference, invitation, place/time information, acceptance with a food offer, seat availability and asking for another photo.
checks.originality_and_names: All scenarios and language are new practice content. Only ordinary personal cast names and generic settings appear. No invented company, institution, address, brand, public policy claim or sourced exercise wording requires an organisation-name search or KNM verification.
checks.images: All nine briefs and alts agree with their tasks and exclude printed text, signage and logos. The configured a1StylePrefix supplies the requested warm paper/gouache style and excludes numerals and watermarks. Every remaining named cast depiction repeats the exact configured traits. Open-task images and alts may supply visible content facts. Opinion and food-choice goals stay open. Pixel quality and exact goal visibility still require rendered-media review.

evidence.sample_omission_proof: The sample asks for another photo and says the learner wants to see it. It does not react to the existing photo.
evidence.natural_variants: Accept any understandable opinion of the existing photo and any request for another one, such as Mag ik nog een foto. Wanting to see another photo does not by itself give an opinion of the current one.
